input.quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 already meets the core preferred position: renewals are 12 months and either party (including us as licensee) can exit on 30 days' written notice, so no walk-away trigger (no multi-year renewals, notice window well under 90 days). Two preferred elements are missing: (i) no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and (ii) no cap on renewal-term price increases — Exhibit B only states "Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]" for maintenance/support and MarketSite fees, leaving renewal uplift unconstrained. The minimal redline adds a 60-day renewal reminder from Commerce One and caps renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% fallback available.

proposal.summary: Add vendor renewal reminder (60 days) and cap renewal fee increases at lesser of CPI and 3%
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 12-month auto-renewal and 30-day non-renewal notice work for us, but we need a renewal reminder from Commerce One and predictable renewal pricing, so we have added a 60-day reminder and capped renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%. If helpful, we can accept a 5% cap instead.

ops.newText: of its intention to terminate this Agreement. Commerce One shall provide Corio with written notice of each upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term. The fees payable for any renewal term shall not exceed the fees payable for the immediately preceding term by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index over such preceding term or (ii) three percent (3%).
